prompt.content:
EVAL: cgh-t02
Implement `weightedEditDistance(a, b)`: the minimum total COST to transform string `a` into string `b`, where an insertion costs 1, a deletion costs 1, and a SUBSTITUTION costs 3. Return a number. Note that a substitution may therefore be more expensive than a delete followed by an insert.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t03
Implement `lastIndexOfSorted(nums, target)`: `nums` is an array of integers sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain duplicates. Return the index of the LAST occurrence of `target`, or -1 if `target` is not present. Return -1 for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t04
Implement `longestCircularRun(nums)`: `nums` is an array of integers treated as CIRCULAR (the element after the last is the first). Return the length of the longest strictly increasing run of CONSECUTIVE elements, where the run may wrap around the end of the array. A run may never use the same array position twice, so the answer can never exceed nums.length. Return 0 for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t05
Implement `allPairSums(nums, target)`: return every pair of INDICES [i, j] with i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] === target. The array may contain duplicate values, and every qualifying index pair must be reported (not just one per value pair). Return the pairs sorted ascending by i, then ascending by j. Return [] when there are none.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t06
Implement `reverseWordsKeepGaps(s)`: split `s` into words (maximal runs of non-space characters) and gaps (maximal runs of space characters). Return a string in which the WORDS appear in reverse order but the SEQUENCE OF GAPS is unchanged — that is, the i-th gap of the output has exactly the same length as the i-th gap of the input, and leading/trailing spaces are preserved in place. Return '' for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t07
Implement `parseRoman(s)`: convert a Roman numeral string to an integer. Only the characters I V X L C D M are valid. The ONLY subtractive pairs permitted are IV IX XL XC CD CM; any other smaller-before-larger pair is invalid. Return -1 for any invalid input, including an empty string, unknown characters, and more than three consecutive identical characters.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-t08
Implement `limitedCoinCombos(coins, amount)`: `coins` is an array of distinct positive integer denominations. Return the number of distinct COMBINATIONS (order does not matter) that sum to exactly `amount`, where each denomination may be used AT MOST TWICE. If amount is 0 the answer is 1 (the empty combination). Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c01
Implement `mergeSpans(spans)`: `spans` is an array of [start, end] integer pairs with start <= end. Merge spans that OVERLAP, where two spans overlap only if they share at least one interior point. Spans that merely TOUCH at an endpoint (one ends exactly where the next begins) do NOT merge. Return the resulting spans sorted ascending by start, then by end. Return [] for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c02
Implement `competitionRank(scores)`: return an array of ranks, one per score, where the highest score has rank 1. Equal scores share the same rank, and the rank of any score is 1 plus the number of scores STRICTLY GREATER than it (so ranks run 1, 2, 2, 4 — not 1, 2, 2, 3). Return [] for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c03
Implement `compressRuns(s)`: compress only runs of 4 OR MORE identical consecutive characters, writing such a run as the character followed by its count in square brackets (five 'a' characters become a[5]). Runs of 1, 2 or 3 characters are copied literally. If `s` contains a '[' or ']' character the input cannot be encoded unambiguously — return null. Return '' for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c04
Implement `balancedOutsideQuotes(s)`: return true when the bracket characters ( ) [ ] { } in `s` are balanced and correctly nested. Bracket characters that appear inside a double-quoted section are IGNORED entirely. A double-quoted section begins at a double-quote character and ends at the next unescaped double-quote. A backslash escapes the character immediately after it anywhere in the string. An unterminated quoted section makes the input invalid — return false. An empty string is balanced.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c05
Implement `trailingAverages(nums, k)`: return an array of the same length as `nums` where element i is the arithmetic mean of the elements from index max(0, i - k + 1) through i inclusive — that is, a trailing window of at most k elements, using however many are available near the start. Return [] for an empty array. If k is less than 1, return null.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c06
Implement `groupAnagrams(words)`: two words belong to the same group when, after lowercasing and discarding every character outside a-z, they contain exactly the same multiset of letters. Within a group, words keep their original input order. Groups are ordered by the input position of their first member. Words that reduce to the empty string all belong to one group together. Return [] for an empty input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c07
Implement `flattenDepth(arr, d)`: return a new array with nested arrays flattened by EXACTLY d levels. d === 0 returns a shallow copy of `arr` (a new array, same elements). d may be Infinity, meaning flatten completely. If d is negative, return null.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c08
Implement `replaceAllSimultaneous(s, pairs)`: `pairs` is an array of [find, replace] string pairs. Perform every replacement SIMULTANEOUSLY in a single left-to-right pass: text produced by a replacement is never itself examined for further matches. At each position, the FIRST pair in `pairs` whose `find` matches wins; scanning then resumes immediately after the matched text. Pairs whose `find` is the empty string are ignored. Return '' for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c09
Implement `addBusinessDays(startDay, n, holidays)`: days are numbered by integers. A day is a WEEKEND when day % 7 is 5 or 6. `holidays` is an array of day numbers that are also non-working. Advance from `startDay` by `n` working days and return the day number reached. `startDay` itself is never counted, whether or not it is a working day. If n is 0, return `startDay` unchanged. n is a non-negative integer.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c10
Implement `parseKeyValues(s)`: parse a string of semicolon-separated segments. Each segment is a key, an equals sign, and a value. Only the FIRST equals sign in a segment splits it, so a value may itself contain equals signs. Whitespace around keys and around values is trimmed. Empty segments (for example from a trailing semicolon) are ignored. A non-empty segment with no equals sign makes the whole input invalid — return null. When a key repeats, the LAST occurrence wins. Return {} for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c11
Implement `dedupeKeepLast(items, key)`: `items` is an array of objects and `key` is a property name. Objects sharing the same value of that property form a group. Return a new array containing one object per group — the LAST object of the group — placed at the position where the FIRST object of that group appeared. Return [] for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-c12
Implement `chunkMinTail(arr, n)`: split `arr` into consecutive chunks of n elements. If the FINAL chunk would contain fewer than ceil(n / 2) elements, merge it into the previous chunk instead of leaving it short. When there is no previous chunk (the array is shorter than n) return that single short chunk as the only chunk. Return [] for an empty array, and null if n is less than 1.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p01
Implement `bankersRound(x, k)`: round the number `x` to `k` decimal places using ROUND-HALF-TO-EVEN — when the part being dropped is exactly half, round to whichever candidate has an even final digit (so at 0 decimals 2.5 becomes 2 and 3.5 becomes 4). Values that are not exactly half round normally. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p02
Implement `sumMoney(amounts)`: `amounts` is an array of USD amounts, each with at most two decimal places, and may include negative values. Return their exact total as a number with at most two decimal places. Binary floating point drift must not appear in the result — adding 0.1 and 0.2 must return exactly 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004. Return 0 for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p03
Implement `sortByKeys(rows, keys)`: `rows` is an array of objects and `keys` is an array of [property, direction] pairs where direction is 'asc' or 'desc'. Sort by each key in turn. Numbers compare numerically, strings compare with the standard less-than operator. The sort must be STABLE: rows that tie on every key keep their original relative order. Return a NEW array; `rows` must not be modified. With an empty `keys` array, return a copy in the original order.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p04
Implement `percentChange(from, to)`: return the percentage change from `from` to `to`, that is (to - from) / from * 100. When `from` is 0 the change is undefined — return null (including when both arguments are 0). Return a number otherwise, and note that a negative `from` still uses the same formula.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p05
Implement `parseDuration(s)`: parse a compact duration such as 1h30m into a total number of SECONDS. The units are d (86400s), h (3600s), m (60s) and s. Each unit may appear at most once and units must appear in that order, largest first. Each value is a non-negative integer. Anything else — an empty string, a bare number with no unit, an unknown unit, a repeated unit, units out of order — is invalid: return null.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p06
Implement `truncateAtWord(s, n)`: shorten `s` so the RETURNED STRING is at most n characters long, counting a three-character ellipsis '...' that is appended whenever anything was cut. If `s` already fits in n characters, return it unchanged with no ellipsis. Otherwise cut at a space so the result never ends mid-word, and drop any whitespace left before the ellipsis. If no space is available inside the budget, cut mid-word instead. If n is less than 3 there is no room for an ellipsis — return the first n characters of `s`. Return null if n is less than 1.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p07
Implement `compareSemver(a, b)`: return -1 if version `a` sorts before `b`, 1 if after, and 0 if they are equal. A version is major.minor.patch, all non-negative integers, optionally followed by a hyphen and a dot-separated prerelease tag. Compare major, then minor, then patch numerically. A version WITH a prerelease sorts BEFORE the same version without one. Prerelease tags compare identifier by identifier: identifiers made only of digits compare numerically and always sort before non-numeric identifiers; other identifiers compare as strings; if all shared identifiers are equal, the tag with MORE identifiers sorts after. If either argument is not a valid version, return null.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p08
Implement `deepEquals(a, b)`: structural equality. Two NaN values ARE equal to each other. Positive and negative zero ARE equal to each other. Values of different types are never equal, so 1 and '1' differ. Arrays are equal when they have the same length and equal elements in order. Plain objects are equal when they have the same set of own keys — order does not matter — and equal values for each. An array is never equal to a plain object. Return a boolean.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p09
Implement `medianNoMutate(nums)`: return the median of an array of numbers. For an even count return the arithmetic mean of the two middle values. The input array MUST NOT be modified in any way — callers rely on its order being preserved. Return null for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cgh-p10
Implement `normalizeWeights(weights)`: scale an array of non-negative numbers so they sum to exactly 1. Each returned value is rounded to 4 decimal places, and because rounding can leave the total slightly off, the LARGEST input's entry absorbs the entire remainder so the returned array sums to exactly 1. If several inputs tie for largest, the earliest one absorbs it. Return null for an empty array or when the inputs sum to 0.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.
